headline: Bitcoin climbed back above $60,000 on Saturday afternoon after crashing to about $55,100 overnight, as traders betting on further falls were forced to buy back.

market.asOf: Read by this desk on Sat 21 Nov: bitcoin from CoinMarketCap at about 15:57 UTC (22:57 Bangkok); ether and solana from Eurasia Business News's Saturday price snapshot, because CoinMarketCap's ether and solana pages served an older copy (no 24-hour change shown for those two). Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 12 out of 100, "Extreme Fear", on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (read at about 15:59 UTC).

stories.title: Bitcoin climbs back above $60,000 after crashing to about $55,100
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest price since September 2024 early on Saturday, then recovered above $60,000 by the afternoon. Traders who had bet on lower prices were forced to close those bets, which means buying bitcoin back, and that added buying pressure.
points: Bitcoin's 24-hour low was $55,126.70 on CoinGlass data, and it then rebounded to about $60,523, per crypto.news.
In a Saturday market snapshot, bitcoin traded at $60,284.42, per Eurasia Business News.
About $2.67 billion of crypto futures bets were wiped out over 24 hours, per CoinGlass data cited by Bitcoin.com News.
In the last hour of crypto.news's CoinGlass reading, $68.82 million of bets on lower prices were closed out against $1.64 million of bets on higher prices.

sources.label: Bitcoin.com News: rebound to $60K after crash near $55K

stories.title: US bitcoin funds lose about $1.25 billion in a week
stories.summary: Money kept flowing out of US spot bitcoin ETFs, the funds that let people buy bitcoin through a normal brokerage account. Friday's figures are still incomplete because BlackRock's fund has not reported, but the week was clearly negative for both bitcoin and ether funds.
points: Bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.25 billion over 16-20 Nov and ether ETFs about $221.7 million, per crypto.news using Farside data.
Friday's posted total was -$124.5 million with BlackRock's IBIT still blank, so it may change, per crypto.news.
Including Friday's provisional figure, November's outflows total about $3.59 billion, which would make it the second-worst month after June 2026, per CryptoTicker.
On Thursday 19 Nov bitcoin ETFs lost $582.2 million, $541.1 million of it from BlackRock's IBIT, per The Block.

stories.title: AI stock rout and Fed hike fears hit crypto company shares
stories.summary: Friday's sell-off in AI and chip stocks spread to crypto-related shares, while traders expect the Fed to raise interest rates in December. US stock markets are closed for the weekend, so these are Friday's closing numbers; Monday's open is the next test.
points: Nvidia closed nearly 14% lower and the Nasdaq 100 fell 5.5% on Friday, per CoinDesk.
Coinbase fell 6.3% to $102.01, Robinhood 9.4% to $62.12 and Strategy (MSTR) 9.7%, per CoinDesk.
Bitcoin miners with AI businesses fell hard: Hut 8 nearly 15%, and Core Scientific, CleanSpark and Bitdeer more than 13% each, per CoinDesk.
A quarter-point Fed hike on 9 Dec is still seen as the most likely outcome, while markets have priced out a half-point hike, per CoinDesk.

briefs.title: Chainflip drained of about $4.86 million
briefs.summary: An attacker drained about $4.86 million from Chainflip's Ethereum vault in a suspected key compromise; its FLIP token fell about 34% and the protocol is in "safe mode", per The Block.

briefs.title: Binance hack funds moving through mixers
briefs.summary: Elliptic says at least 2,310 BTC (about $149 million) from the Binance hack has gone through coinjoin mixers, about 90% of it since Tuesday, per The Block.

briefs.title: Saylor says Strategy could shrink its STRC preferred shares
briefs.summary: Michael Saylor said Strategy could let STRC shrink from about $7.7 billion to about $5 billion and keep its dividend at 12% for December, per Cryptonews.net.

briefs.title: JPMorgan: bitcoin trades far below its mining cost
briefs.summary: JPMorgan estimates it costs about $86,000 to produce one bitcoin and says "some capital has also left the crypto market altogether," per The Block.

briefs.title: Altcoins hit harder than bitcoin on Friday
briefs.summary: Ether fell 7%, Hyperliquid 8% and zcash 14% on Friday, per CoinDesk.
